title: Set Operations, Power Sets & Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion
outcomes: Apply the two-set Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion |A U B| = |A| + |B| - |A n B| to avoid double-counting overlaps.
Compute the exact cardinality 2^n of a finite power set P(A) and count proper or non-empty proper subsets 2^n - 2.
Generalize Inclusion-Exclusion to three finite sets by adding back the triple intersection |A n B n C|.

sections.intuition: Sets are the foundational vocabulary of modern mathematics. When we form a subset S ⊆ A of an n-element set A, each of the n elements independently has 2 choices (either in S or not in S), so the power set P(A) has exactly 2^n subsets—including the empty set ∅ and the full set A itself. When counting the union A ∪ B of two overlapping sets, simply adding |A| + |B| counts every element in the intersection A ∩ B twice; subtracting |A ∩ B| once ensures every element is counted with multiplicity 1.
sections.formal_definition:
1. Power Set & Proper Subsets: For a finite set A with |A| = n, the power set P(A) = {S : S ⊆ A} has cardinality |P(A)| = 2^n. A has 2^n - 1 proper subsets (S ⊂ A, S ≠ A) and 2^n - 2 non-empty proper subsets (S ≠ ∅ and S ≠ A).
2. Two-Set Inclusion-Exclusion: |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| - |A ∩ B|.
3. Three-Set Inclusion-Exclusion: |A ∪ B ∪ C| = (|A| + |B| + |C|) - (|A ∩ B| + |A ∩ C| + |B ∩ C|) + |A ∩ B ∩ C|.
sections.worked_example:
Suppose |A| = 15, |B| = 14, |C| = 13, |A ∩ B| = 6, |A ∩ C| = 5, |B ∩ C| = 4, and |A ∩ B ∩ C| = 2. Find |A ∪ B ∪ C|.
1. Sum the singletons: 15 + 14 + 13 = 42.
2. Subtract the pairwise overlaps: 42 - (6 + 5 + 4) = 42 - 15 = 27.
3. Notice an element in A ∩ B ∩ C was added 3 times in Step 1 and subtracted 3 times in Step 2 (net count 0); add |A ∩ B ∩ C| = 2 back: 27 + 2 = 29.
common_misconceptions: Adding |A| + |B| without subtracting |A ∩ B| when A and B are not disjoint.
Forgetting that the empty set ∅ is a subset of every set A (so excluding both ∅ and A leaves 2^n - 2 subsets).
Subtracting |A ∩ B ∩ C| instead of adding it back in the three-set Inclusion-Exclusion formula.
